stories.summary: As electronic components shrink and increase in power, heat dissipation has become a primary concern for performance and reliability. Thermally conductive plastics are being positioned as a potential solution to manage these thermal loads. Excessive heat remains a persistent challenge for the longevity of modern hardware.

stories.summary: Research published in Resources, Environment and Sustainability indicates that replacing polyethylene packaging with paper, glass, aluminum, or steel could increase environmental impacts. The study emphasizes the necessity of region-specific life cycle assessments. Science-based decision-making is recommended when evaluating strategies to reduce the global warming potential of packaging.

stories.title: Vitrimers proposed as solution for thermoset plastic recycling
stories.summary: A comment in the Journal of Materials Science: Composites suggests vitrimers could bridge the recycling gap between thermoplastics and thermosets. These polymers use Covalent Adaptable Networks to combine structural stability with reprocessability. The authors argue this hybrid architecture provides a foundation for achieving closed-loop circularity in polymer manufacturing.

stories.title: Ahmedabad recycler NEPRA raises Rs 110 crore
stories.summary: Ahmedabad-based NEPRA has raised Rs 110 crore in equity from the Private Infrastructure Development Group. The company, which calls itself India's largest dry waste recycling firm, plans to use the capital to build new material recovery facilities and expand its plastic recycling capacity. Recycling is now an asset class.

stories.title: Chemical recycling faces inorganic hurdles
stories.summary: A study in Nature Chemical Engineering finds that inorganic contaminants in post-consumer plastic waste significantly alter catalytic activity during chemical recycling. Researchers testing zeolite catalysts identified that common impurities act as poisons, imposing severe operational constraints on the process. The chemistry of trash remains complicated.

stories.title: Recyclers target food-grade polypropylene supply
stories.summary: WM has signed an annual 25-million-pound offtake agreement with PureCycle for food-grade resin. Meanwhile, Republic Services is seeking regulatory approval to expand the use of its post-consumer polypropylene in food packaging applications. The industry is attempting to turn old containers into new ones.

stories.title: Bath researchers receive £1.7 million for acrylic recycling
stories.summary: The University of Bath has secured a £1.7 million grant from the EPSRC and Defra to develop scalable technologies for recycling Perspex. The project builds on previous work demonstrating the recovery of high-quality material without conventional environmental costs. The team is now moving toward industrial application.

stories.title: Advanced recycling enters the conversation
stories.summary: The R Street Institute suggests that advanced recycling merits experimentation as a method to manage non-biodegradable plastic waste. While noting that plastics are ubiquitous in modern life, the report frames the technology as a potential solution for materials that do not naturally degrade. Experimentation is ongoing.

Bombay High Court orders Kanjurmarg waste audit
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court has directed a committee to conduct an internal audit of the Kanjurmarg dumping facility to address odour and public health concerns. The court highlighted plastic as a major ecological challenge and encouraged citizens to improve waste segregation. The facility handles 7,000 tonnes of waste daily.

stories.title: EU bans plastic waste exports to non-OECD nations
stories.summary: The European Union will prohibit plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries starting 21 November 2026. The move aims to strengthen the circular economy and reduce pollution, affecting up to 1.5 million tonnes of annual exports. The EU generates 40 million tonnes of plastic waste each year.

stories.title: EU plastic export ban takes effect in November
stories.summary: From 21 November 2026, the EU will ban plastic waste exports to non-OECD countries under new Waste Shipment Regulations. The measure, which lasts until at least May 2029, is part of a broader effort to manage the 40 million tonnes of plastic waste the bloc produces annually.

stories.title: Delhi introduces new waste management fines
stories.summary: Delhi's 2026 bye-laws propose fines of up to Rs 1.5 lakh for waste management violations. Burning garbage in the open will cost Rs 10,000, while littering carries a Rs 1,000 penalty. The rules target residents, businesses, and institutions to curb improper disposal and packaging practices.

stories.title: Trade groups challenge California EPR law
stories.summary: The Flexible Packaging Association and the American Forest and Paper Association are seeking an injunction against California's Extended Producer Responsibility program. The groups are part of a lawsuit challenging the state's recyclability labeling requirements. The legal dispute over packaging continues.

stories.title: Packaging Federation welcomes PFAS policy shift
stories.summary: The Packaging Federation has expressed relief after PackUK reversed a decision to automatically assign Red ratings to packaging containing trace PFAS. The Federation warned that the original proposal would have significantly increased costs for producers and retailers across complex global supply chains. Financial stability is the priority.

stories.title: PackUK reverts to intentional PFAS classification
stories.summary: PackUK has agreed to return to its previous Recyclability Assessment Methodology regarding PFAS. Packaging will now only receive an automatic Red-rating if the chemicals were intentionally added. The change follows industry pushback against the higher fees associated with the Red classification under the EPR system.

stories.title: PackUK proposes higher EPR fee multipliers
stories.summary: PackUK has proposed increasing the fee multiplier for Red-rated packaging to 2.0 for 2027/28 and 2.4 for 2028/29. The proposal aims to fund discounts for more recyclable materials. Producers may face higher costs for decisions made during 2026. The cost of being Red is rising.

stories.title: PackUK plans faster EPR fee hikes
stories.summary: PackUK proposes accelerating fee increases for hard-to-recycle packaging to subsidize discounts for sustainable alternatives. Under the draft, Red-rated packaging fees would reach 2.4 times the base rate by 2028/29. The current multiplier for 2026/27 remains at 1.2. The price of non-recyclability is being adjusted.

stories.title: EU packaging law impacts small record labels
stories.summary: The EU's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation now requires small record labels and mail-order businesses to manage cross-border Extended Producer Responsibility duties. The law, which took effect 12 August 2026, adds new administrative layers for those selling CDs and vinyl across European borders.

stories.title: Plant-based coating developed for coffee cups
stories.summary: University of Waterloo researchers have created a cellulose-based coating that replaces plastic liners in disposable coffee cups. The material resists boiling water and oils, potentially simplifying paper recycling by removing the need to separate plastic layers. The design allows for thinner paper usage.

stories.title: Study finds paper packaging can increase emissions
stories.summary: Replacing single-use polyethylene with paper, glass, aluminium or steel alternatives increased potential greenhouse gas emissions by 190% in the United States and 50% in Europe, according to a new life cycle assessment. The substitutions also increased packaging weight by up to sixfold. Physics remains a stubborn constraint.

stories.title: ITC shifts focus toward proprietary paperboard coatings
stories.summary: ITC is developing proprietary coatings for paperboard to replace plastic components in coffee cups and pods. Chairman Sanjiv Puri says the company is moving its narrative toward sustainable packaging through these new technologies, aiming to replace plastic lids and pods with moulded fibre products made from paperboard.

stories.title: Recycled white lined chipboard market sees growth
stories.summary: The recycled white lined chipboard industry is expanding as sustainability and cost-effectiveness become priorities for the food and beverage sector. Market growth is driven by shifting consumer preferences toward eco-friendly packaging, with the industry currently exploring new valuation trends and segmentation to support its ongoing expansion efforts.

stories.title: Corrugated packaging market expected to reach USD 444.3 billion
stories.summary: The global corrugated packaging market is projected to reach USD 444.3 billion by 2032, up from USD 324.2 billion in 2025, according to Persistence Market Research. The sector, which uses fluted paperboard layers for protective packaging, continues to balance material costs with evolving sustainability requirements for distribution.

stories.summary: The global carton erectors market is transitioning from standardized high-volume systems to flexible, intelligent solutions, according to IndexBox. The sector, which provides automated machinery for forming corrugated boxes, is seeing growth driven by e-commerce automation and the need to handle diverse packaging formats and fluctuating demand.

stories.summary: The global box making machines market is expected to see demand propelled by structural shifts in retail and logistics through 2035, according to IndexBox. stories.summary: The global paper roll clamps market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture, according to IndexBox. stories.summary: UK-based corrugated packaging manufacturer Durham Box has upgraded its gluing controllers to the Xtend3 generation and installed an Xmelt hot melt system from Baumer hhs. stories.title: Atlantic Zeiser to debut automated card packaging system
stories.summary: Atlantic Zeiser will introduce its COBOMASTER system at TRUSTECH 2026. The machine automates the process of inserting personalized cards into finished packages, a task the company identifies as a production bottleneck due to repetitive manual labor. It includes robotic insertion, automated closing and optional secondary packaging features.

stories.title: Clarissa Group enters FMCG market with platform launch
stories.summary: Clarissa Group has diversified from luxury hospitality and real estate into the fast-moving consumer goods sector with the launch of Clarissa Fresh. The platform will source and distribute fresh produce and daily essentials, focusing on supply chain reliability and product quality for both individual and institutional buyers.

stories.title: Fyffes reduces plastic in banana packaging
stories.summary: Fyffes is introducing a banana packing system that uses 46% less plastic per container, a change the company says saves 16kg of plastic per unit. The firm has not disclosed how many containers will use the new system or the total annual plastic reduction. The plastic is gone.

stories.title: Managing holiday packaging waste
stories.summary: Retailers often treat the surge of holiday cardboard as an afterthought, leading to overflowing loading docks by the time the season peaks. Experts suggest that effective waste management requires planning months before Black Friday. Cardboard does not stop growing just because the holiday season is busy.

stories.summary: TCPL Packaging has entered a joint venture with Italian firm Brandart to expand into the Asia-Pacific region. Existing partners will retain 24.5% each and continue to share control of the partnership with the laminate manufacturer.

stories.title: NMC acquires foam manufacturer PTI
stories.summary: NMC has completed its acquisition of North American foam manufacturer PTI. The deal is intended to strengthen the company's regional presence. NMC will retain local leadership and existing operations as part of the integration process.

stories.title: EPL plans 1,000 crore investment for acquisitions
stories.summary: Flexible packaging maker EPL is setting aside 1,000 crore rupees for acquisitions as it aims to build a 20,000 crore global FMCG packaging business within five years. The company currently manufactures tubes for brands including Colgate and L’Oreal. It is also merging with Singapore-based Indovida.

Label Apeel targets growth after investment

The business is now managed by the second and third generations of the founding family.
